leading_positions.synthesis: Four of six members explicitly prefer Anne Carson as sole laureate. The count equals the four-vote threshold, but this is a round 1 position and not a decision. All four ground the case in a recognizable voice, formal invention in Autobiography of Red and Nox, and long engagement with Greek and Latin literature. Several also note that writing in English lets linguistic achievement be judged without translation. The four citations differ in emphasis: hybrid forms and dialogue with antiquity (Carlberg, Swärd), renewal of lyric, narrative and essay with genre boundaries dissolved (Palm), and extending the book as a literary form (Olsson). Every B002 supporter lists the same reservations: reputation may rest on a few landmark books, and translations, scholarship and book-object work are hard to weigh against original creation. No supporter claims to have verified the whole corpus. The chair is among the B002 supporters, which is disclosed here and not adjudicated.

Two of six members explicitly prefer Mircea Cărtărescu as sole laureate, and both propose near-identical citations naming prose and poetry in Romanian as a visionary, densely patterned metaphysical architecture. They rest the case on a recognizable voice and on the scale and coherence of the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid as one sustained project. Both state that they judge the Romanian prose through translation. Both name recurring motifs that may be repetition and not development as the main open risk. Both list Carson (B002) and Murnane (B001) as alternatives. Neither treats agreement between them as independent evidence of merit. They differ from the B002 group mainly on where the more durable and more securely assessable oeuvre lies.

areas_of_agreement: All six members name both Carson (B002) and Cărtărescu (B036) in their preferred configuration or alternatives. Each also proposes only a single writer, with no multiwriter configuration.

All six describe both candidates as having a distinctive, recognizable voice and real formal and imaginative achievement. The disagreement is about relative sustained quality and scope, not about whether either belongs among the strongest candidates.

Members who discuss a Carson citation converge on anchoring it in her original written work (verse novel, lyric, elegy, essays). They treat translations and scholarship as context showing the depth of her engagement with antiquity, not as credited achievements. Where wording differs, as in some colleagues' paraphrases of the chair's earlier position, the difference is described as one of framing.

Every member acknowledges that their knowledge rests on public information and not on verified reading of full corpora. Every member also states translation limits for non-English candidates, and none claims independent source verification.
No member reports a documented conflict connecting them to a shortlisted writer.
scientific_disputes: Whether Carson's hybrid, genre-crossing and book-object mode is a core literary achievement within Nobel's will or a peripheral one. Sem-Sandberg is the most doubtful. Carlberg, Olsson, Palm and Swärd argue that the written language carries the work and that the contested genre labels are part of what she renews.

Whether Cărtărescu's recurring imagery and obsessions are structural development or repetition across his long novels. Mattson, Sem-Sandberg, Carlberg, Olsson, Palm and Swärd each raise the point, and none can settle it from public knowledge or translations.

Whether sustained quality is better shown by one long, coherent project (Cărtărescu) or by renewal of form across genres (Carson). Mattson and Sem-Sandberg weigh the first more heavily. The four B002 supporters weigh the second more heavily and see variation of method as part of the achievement.

How far Cărtărescu's linguistic achievement is the writer's own and how far it is carried by translation. Palm and Swärd say they can judge Carson's English directly. Swärd also notes that this asymmetry may inflate her confidence in Carson relative to translated writers.

Secondary candidates are not shared. Murnane (B001) is an alternative for Mattson and Sem-Sandberg, who both note his narrow range. Adonis (B014) is an alternative only for Olsson, and Swärd says she cannot judge his prosody in translation well enough to defend him. Robinson (B020) is an alternative for Palm, whose compact corpus is compared with Carson's. Tawada (B015) is an alternative for Carlberg and Can Xue (B007) for Swärd.
attribution_disputes: For Carson, how to scope the citation so that translations, classical adaptations, scholarship and performance or book-object works are not credited as the core original creation. Several members say the citation text itself should draw this boundary.

Whether the physical or visual form of Nox can be credited as literary achievement. Sem-Sandberg says he cannot judge its material dimension from description. The B002 supporters would rest the citation on the written text, naming form only as method or as an extension of the book.

The proposed citations differ in wording and scope: Carson's ranges from hybrid forms and antiquity, through genre boundaries dissolved, to extending the book as a literary form. Cărtărescu's names prose and poetry together. Translation coverage of his poetry and early prose is uncertain, so the poetry part of that citation rests on less evidence.
No member disputes the identity of either candidate or proposes any credited name beyond a single writer.
maturity_disputes: Whether Carson's standing rests on a few landmark books (Autobiography of Red, Nox) or on a body of work sustained across decades. Carlberg, Palm and Swärd say they cannot verify quality book by book for mid-career, later and shorter works. The chair says the same about later books and asks that the corpus be tested.
Whether Cărtărescu's late novels have kept developing, and whether his poetry and early prose add weight. Translation coverage is unverified for both.

Whether compact corpora (Robinson, Murnane) or very large ones show sustained quality and breadth of significance more securely. Murnane's range is described as narrow, and the chair finds Robinson's breadth less settled than Carson's or Cărtărescu's.
For Adonis, Can Xue and Tawada, members state that the relation between formative and later work and the quality of the originals cannot be judged from translation.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Carlberg is a co-opted member whose actual committee voting status is undocumented. Her B002 preference is counted as a simulated vote under a modeling assumption, and the four-supporter count for B002 depends on it.
The chair (Olsson) is one of the four B002 supporters while also writing this summary. His own scholarly work on poetry, the fragment and exile is context only.

Sem-Sandberg discloses a thematic proximity to the Central and Eastern European tradition from his own work. Mattson, Palm, Swärd and Carlberg describe their own literary practice or connections as context only. No documented personal, institutional or professional tie to any shortlisted writer is reported by any member.
No recusal is requested by any member. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
questions_for_round2: Can the Carson supporters and the Cărtărescu supporters agree on a citation text for B002 that names only original written work (verse novel, lyric, elegy, essays) and treats translations and scholarship as context? If so, would Mattson and Sem-Sandberg regard that scope as resolving their objection about hybrid and book-object works?

Which Carson books beyond Autobiography of Red and Nox should carry the sustained-quality claim, and can B002 supporters say what in the mid-career and later work reaches the same level? Which parts should the citation leave out?

For Cărtărescu, which specific volumes, and which translations of his poetry and early prose, should the committee compare to decide whether recurring imagery is development or repetition? Would an external reading of the Romanian originals be needed, and what finding would move B002 supporters toward B036 or the reverse?

Does anyone wish to change a first preference after round 1? If Carson's case is narrowed to original written work, does it still outweigh the claim for a single long project? What would each B036 supporter need in order to rank B002 first?

Do Mattson, Sem-Sandberg or any other member want Murnane (B001), Adonis (B014), Robinson (B020) or Tawada (B015) examined more closely as a challenger, and on what evidence of sustained quality and linguistic achievement, given the translation limits already stated?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two clustered positions on the same two writers, Carson (four explicit first preferences, including the chair's) and Cărtărescu (two), with every member naming both among their top choices. The shared uncertainties are the scope of a Carson citation, whether Cărtărescu's recurrences amount to development, and how far translation limits what can be judged. The B002 count meets the four-vote threshold only if the simulated vote of the co-opted member is assumed. This summary is a neutral record of positions stated in the round 1 files, not a ruling.
